title: The reconciler's own origin reads are now the suite's biggest measured git cost
description:
After the store's write path went through one fast-import per step, the biggest measured git cost in internal/reconcile's slowest tests is the cluster of origin reads around the CAS: the store's peek triple (fetch + rev-parse + ls-tree) and repoGit's fetch/ls-remote/rev-parse reads. A wrapper-counted run of the two heaviest store-touching tests (TestAQuietGateIsWarnedAboutAndATalkativeOneIsNot, TestTheWaitUsesTheExecutorsCadenceNotTheRuns) counts 597 fetches, 893 rev-parses, 268 ls-remotes and 357 ls-trees of 5039 invocations. Each is a deliberate freshness point in the compare-and-swap, so the cut is a design question (what may read origin through another reader's fetch, and what must still ask origin itself), not a mechanical one. Measured against A1: the reconcile suite now runs 293 min serial on this host (was 337) and the halving A1 asks for is not reachable while this cluster stands.
evidence: internal/reconcile/git.go:93 (repoGit's spawn) and internal/runstate/store.go:377 (peek); wrapper-counted profile: 2115 of 5039 invocations in the two heaviest store-touching tests
